claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

apprenticeship_location.description: The country where the child has started an apprenticeship, where relevant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child I'm asking about - my son Alex. He's 17 and lives with me here at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to ask you a few more questions about Alex to determine your eligibility.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he in school, college, sixth form, or an approved training program?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in school or college anymore. He actually started an apprenticeship in Wales recently.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to clarify one important detail:

**Is Alex's apprenticeship in England, or is it in Wales?** 

(The reason I ask is that the rules specifically mention apprenticeships in England as affecting eligibility, and I want to make sure I understand your situation correctly.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's in Wales - he's doing his apprenticeship there.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I have a few more questions to complete my assessment:

1. **First, do you live in the UK?**

2. And just to confirm - **are you currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex, or are you looking to apply for it?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm here with Alex. And no, I'm not currently receiving Child Benefit for him. That's why I'm asking - I want to know if I can apply for it now that he's doing this apprenticeship.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I need to understand one more important detail about Alex's apprenticeship:

**How many hours per week is Alex working in his apprenticeship?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's working full-time - it's a proper apprenticeship, so he's there all week during working hours.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me make sure I understand the situation correctly:

**When you say "full-time" and "all week during working hours," does that mean Alex is working 24 hours or more per week in his apprenticeship?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - he's working more than 24 hours a week. It's a full-time apprenticeship program.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why: While Alex is 17 years old (under 20), which would normally allow Child Benefit to continue if he were in approved education or training, the rules state that Child Benefit stops when a child starts paid work for 24 hours or more per week and is no longer in approved education or training.

Since Alex is working more than 24 hours per week in his full-time apprenticeship, you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for him.

I understand this may not be the answer you were hoping for, but I hope this clarifies your situation. If Alex's circumstances change in the future (for example, if he returns to full-time education), you may want to reassess your eligibility at that time.
